Loss ratio = mean squared error of the second model / mean squared error of the first; below 1 favours the second model. 95% CI: moving-block bootstrap over origin months of the ratio of monthly mean losses. p: one-sided HLN-corrected Diebold-Mariano test that the second model has lower loss, computed on the monthly mean loss differential pooled over all series. Primary timing: price release lag 1 month(s).

**Outcome: no established improvement.** None of the 8 confirmatory tests was significant after the Holm adjustment (0 of 8 point ratios were below 1). The study establishes no improvement from production-region weather. This is not evidence that weather has no effect: with roughly 65 monthly observations, improvements of a few percent in loss cannot be detected.
